step1_figure.description: Figure 13.17 shows a cross-coupled inverter latch loaded with two 50 fF capacitors at nodes In and Out to simulate the delay and behavior associated with metastability when initialized near VDD/2.

switching_point_voltage.description: Inverter switching point voltage (Vsp) where Vin = Vout, representing the metastable operating point of the cross-coupled pair

equation.formula: V_SP = (VDD - |Vthp| + sqrt(beta_n / beta_p) * Vthn) / (1 + sqrt(beta_n / beta_p))
equation.explanation: At the switching point, both PMOS and NMOS are in saturation with equal drain currents, setting the metastable voltage where positive feedback initiates.
equation.assumptions: Both transistors in saturation; lambda channel-length modulation neglected for first-order Vsp calculation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard CMOS inverters with PMOS/NMOS sizing ratio around 2:1 place Vsp slightly below VDD/2 due to higher electron mobility.

metastability_resolution_time.description: Time required for the cross-coupled nodes to escape the metastable state and transition to valid logic levels (10% to 90% VDD)

equation.formula: t_resolve = tau * ln(VDD / (2 * delta_V0)), where tau = C_load / gm
equation.explanation: Due to positive feedback around the cross-coupled loop, an initial differential voltage delta_V0 grows exponentially with time constant tau until reaching rail voltages.
equation.assumptions: C_load = 50 fF on each node as drawn in Fig. 13.17; initial voltage perturbation delta_V0 = 1 mV from metastable point.

sky130_expected.calculation: At V_SP ≈ 0.85 V, gm = gmn + gmp ≈ 1.58 mA/V. tau = C_load / gm = 50 fF / 1.58 mA/V ≈ 31.6 ps. For delta_V0 = 1 mV, ln((VDD/2)/delta_V0) = ln(900) ≈ 6.8, yielding an intrinsic regeneration delay of ~0.22 ns. With finite slew rate and settling in layout/models, Baker observes ~2.5 ns in Fig 13.17 simulation.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Baker explicitly notes on page 384: 'It takes approximately 2.5 ns for the In/Out signals to change states' under 50 fF load.

small_signal_loop_gain.description: Small-signal open-loop voltage gain around the regenerative loop at the metastable point

equation.explanation: The regeneration speed depends directly on the gain around the feedback loop. Higher gain shortens metastability delay and sharpens the butterfly curve transition.
equation.assumptions: Small-signal model evaluated at the metastable operating point V_SP.

sky130_expected.calculation: At ID ≈ 180 uA, ro_n || ro_p = 1 / ((lambda_n + lambda_p) * ID) = 1 / (0.2 * 180u) ≈ 27.8 kOhm. Single inverter gain |Av| = gm * ro = 1.58m * 27.8k ≈ 43.9 (32.8 dB). Loop gain T = Av^2 ≈ 1930 (65.7 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Two cascaded submicron CMOS inverters biased in high-gain saturation provide 50 to 70 dB of loop gain.

output_high_voltage.description: Output high voltage level (VOH) after resolving to the stable logic state

equation.explanation: In full CMOS static cross-coupled inverters, PMOS pulls up fully to VDD when the opposing NMOS turns off.
equation.assumptions: No resistive load connected to ground.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Static CMOS logic achieves rail-to-rail voltage swing.

output_low_voltage.description: Output low voltage level (VOL) after resolving to the stable logic state

equation.explanation: In full CMOS static cross-coupled inverters, NMOS pulls down fully to 0 V when the opposing PMOS turns off.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Static CMOS pull-down brings the node to ground.

metastable_current.description: Direct-path supply current drawn by the latch while lingering at the metastable state

source.reference: Page 385 text (contention and wasted current at metastable state)

equation.explanation: While both inverters are at V_SP, both PMOS and NMOS in each inverter are conducting direct saturation current.
equation.assumptions: Both inverters identical and symmetrically biased at V_SP.

sky130_expected.calculation: For one inverter: I_D ≈ 0.5 * 2.7m * (0.85 - 0.42)^2 ≈ 250 uA. For two inverters: I_DD,meta = 2 * 250 uA ≈ 500 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct-path current peaks near VDD/2 when both NMOS and PMOS channels are fully open.

step3_testbench.description: Transient and operating point testbench for the cross-coupled inverter latch under 50 fF capacitive load, simulating metastability resolution delay as depicted in Figure 13.17.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Cross-Coupled Inverter Latch Metastability Simulation (Fig 13.17)
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=1.5u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=3.0u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=1.5u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=3.0u L_xm4=0.15u

* DUT - Cross-coupled inverters with 50fF capacitors
xm1 Vout Vin 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm3 Vin Vout 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 Vin Vout VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
C1 Vout 0 5e-14
C2 Vin 0 5e-14

* Initial condition placed near metastable switching point (VDD/2 = 0.9V)
* with a tiny 0.5mV perturbation to trigger resolution
.ic v(Vin)=0.9005 v(Vout)=0.8995

.control
* Run transient analysis for 4ns as in Fig 13.17
tran 10p 4n uic

* Measure final resolved logic levels
meas tran voh max v(Vin)
meas tran vol min v(Vout)

* Measure resolution time to reach valid logic levels (10% to 90% of VDD)
meas tran t_resolve trig v(Vin) val=0.95 rise=1 targ v(Vin) val=1.62 rise=1

* Measure peak supply current during metastable state
let idd = -i(VDD)
meas tran idd_meta max idd

* Measure switching point voltage at t=0
meas tran v_sp find v(Vin) at=10p

print voh vol t_resolve idd_meta v_sp
plot v(Vin) v(Vout)

quit
.endc
.end
